content.user_title: Build Mock API Servers for Tests
content.value_statement: Teams need stable APIs before backend services are ready. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code design mock REST, GraphQL, and OpenAPI servers.
actual_capabilities: Generates mock REST endpoint plans with success, validation, auth, and error responses.
Shows setup patterns for JSON Server, MSW, Prism, Express, Apollo Server, WireMock, and Faker.
Designs scenarios for delays, timeouts, rate limits, network errors, and conditional responses.
Helps create mock data models for users, posts, authentication flows, and CRUD operations.
Compares mock server tools by complexity, best fit, and feature coverage.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples; it does not host a server by itself.
Generated mocks must be reviewed before use with real credentials or production data.
OpenAPI behavior depends on the quality and completeness of the supplied specification.
Some examples require installing third-party packages or Docker images.

use_cases.title: Unblock Frontend Development
use_cases.description: Create predictable REST endpoints while backend services are still in progress.

use_cases.title: Test Failure Paths
use_cases.description: Simulate validation errors, auth failures, slow responses, timeouts, and rate limits.

use_cases.title: Validate API Contracts
use_cases.description: Turn OpenAPI or GraphQL plans into mock behavior for early client testing.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Mock API
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple mock users API for local frontend development. Include endpoints, response states, and the best tool choice.

prompt_templates.title: Mock Error and Delay States
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend my mock API with slow responses, validation errors, auth failures, rate limits, and network failures for testing.

prompt_templates.title: Generate From OpenAPI
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this OpenAPI summary and propose a Prism or MSW mock plan with endpoint coverage and test scenarios.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Stateful GraphQL Mock
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a stateful GraphQL mock server for users and posts. Include mutations, resolver behavior, data reset steps, and testing boundaries.

output_examples.input: I need a mock users service for a React app.
output: Endpoints cover list, detail, create, update, delete, and login.
The response matrix includes success, validation failure, unauthorized, not found, and timeout cases.

output_examples.input: QA needs failure scenarios before the backend is complete.
output: A test plan covers slow responses, network errors, bad input, expired auth, and rate limits.
Each scenario includes expected status, user impact, and reset guidance.

output_examples.input: Choose a mock server tool for an OpenAPI project.
output: Prism is recommended for contract-first mocks.
MSW is recommended when tests need browser or Node request interception.
WireMock is recommended when the team needs advanced request matching.

best_practices: Keep mock endpoints aligned with the current API contract.
Use realistic data while replacing secrets and personal data with safe test values.
Reset state between tests so results stay repeatable.
anti_patterns: Using production credentials, tokens, or customer records in mock data.
Letting mock behavior drift from the real API contract.
Running global installs or container images without reviewing package sources and versions.

faq.question: Can this skill create REST mocks?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides REST mocks with endpoints, methods, responses, validation errors, and local server options.

faq.question: Can it support GraphQL mocks?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes GraphQL mock server patterns with schemas, resolvers, mock data, and mutation behavior.

faq.question: Does it run a hosted mock server?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions and examples that you can adapt in your own development environment.

faq.question: Which tools does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers JSON Server, MSW, Prism, Express, Apollo Server, WireMock, and Faker-based data generation.

faq.question: Is it useful for automated tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps design stable mocks for unit tests, integration tests, auth checks, and failure-path testing.

faq.question: Should I use real production data?
faq.answer: No. Use sanitized test data and placeholder credentials when building mock responses or replay scenarios.
